entry.title: BTCPay Server Urges Shutdown After Reports of Hot-Wallet Sweeps
entry.summary:
BTCPay Server, the open-source self-hosted Bitcoin payment processor, advised operators to shut down their instances after reports that hot wallets tied to the software were being swept, indicating an active security incident affecting Bitcoin merchants. The project's guidance also directed operators to update to version 2.4.2, which refreshes LND and regenerates its admin macaroon.
Merchants running their own BTCPay instances hold the keys to the funds those servers control, so an active draining incident exposes them to direct loss until they shut down or update. BTCPay is a widely used self-hosted alternative to custodial payment processors, giving the advisory an unusually large operational footprint.
The incident appears tied to a Lightning credential flaw in versions before 2.4.2 that let attackers obtain the credentials controlling a store's Lightning funds. The project said operators unsure whether an update applied correctly should re-run it via the user interface or btcpay-update.sh; the exact loss magnitude and root cause have not been resolved in reporting.

entry.title: Cybersecurity Stocks In Focus After Binance Hack Raises Digital Asset Security Questions
entry.summary:
Simply Wall St published a market commentary item flagging cybersecurity stocks as a focus of attention after a hack at Binance renewed concerns about digital-asset security and exchange safeguards. The piece is secondary stock-market commentary rather than primary incident reporting, and it does not establish the size of the loss or the number of users affected.
The item links an exchange security failure to investor attention on listed cybersecurity vendors, framing crypto-incident risk as a potential demand driver for that sector.
Other reporting surfaced in search results describes a 2026 Binance breach as the largest-ever cryptocurrency heist, surpassing the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, with investors withdrawing $3.6 billion in funds; those figures come from separate outlets and are not part of the Simply Wall St commentary.

entry.title: b14g Suffers Unauthorized Withdrawal of 97 Million CORE, Pauses Contracts and Freezes Some Funds
entry.summary:
b14g, a Bitcoin dual-staking layer, said that at 17:29 Beijing time on October 31, roughly 97 million CORE tokens staked through its protocol were withdrawn without authorization and transferred to an attacker's address. The protocol said it immediately paused the affected contracts and is working with the Core team, security partners and exchanges to trace the funds and coordinate freezes and recovery.
Core DAO said the vulnerability affecting b14g does not affect the Core network itself: consensus, validators and staking contracts ran normally throughout, and CORE staked directly with validators or through other protocols is unaffected. Tracking shows about 68 million CORE is still on the Core chain, with exchanges having frozen roughly 9 million CORE tied to the incident.
CryptoSlate reported that "zero-token withdrawals" allowed the attacker to drain the CORE from the Bitcoin staking platform. Recovery is still in progress: the roughly 9 million CORE frozen by exchanges is a partial amount, and the majority of the funds remains on-chain rather than recovered.

entry.title: Two cross-chain bridges in the SOON ecosystem see abnormal withdrawals; officials suspend service and open investigation
entry.summary:
SOON Foundation said that at roughly 11:00 UTC on 31 October 2026, abnormal withdrawal activity occurred on the svmBNB and SOON Mainnet cross-chain bridges. The foundation detected the anomaly at 14:00 UTC that day and immediately shut down the bridging services, saying both bridges remain under its control and will stay offline pending an investigation.
The halt freezes cross-chain movement between svmBNB and SOON Mainnet while the foundation investigates, leaving users unable to bridge assets through either route.
The announcement did not disclose the scale of assets involved in the abnormal withdrawals or any specific losses. SOON said it will publish further information as the investigation progresses.

entry.title: Coinbase's Third-Party Vendor Problem Strikes Again With Amplitude Leak
entry.summary:
Coinbase acknowledged a security incident at Amplitude, its third-party product analytics provider, which exposed contact information belonging to a small subset of Coinbase customers alongside other Amplitude customers. Coinbase says its own platform was not breached, and the company has pushed back on circulating claims that 70,000 users were affected.
The incident extends a pattern the source headline frames as recurring for Coinbase: customer data leaving the exchange through outside vendors rather than through a breach of Coinbase's own systems. Exposed contact details give attackers material for phishing and social-engineering attempts aimed at exchange users.
According to The CyberSec Guru, Coinbase disclosed the Amplitude incident on October 28. Reporting also notes that Coinbase's position is that it "has not had a data breach," with the impact attributed to Amplitude and limited to a small subset of customer contact data.

entry.title: Bitcoin redemption freeze puts $136 million Aave market under scrutiny
entry.summary:
A freeze on Bitcoin redemptions has put an Aave lending market holding roughly $136 million in exposure under scrutiny, according to CryptoSlate. The halt raises questions about the solvency of the Bitcoin-pegged asset's issuer and the quality of collateral backing that market.
If holders of the affected Bitcoin-pegged asset cannot redeem it for native BTC, the collateral backing loans on that Aave market may be worth less than its on-chain price implies, exposing lenders on that market to potential shortfalls.
The $136 million figure refers to the size of the Aave market's exposure, not a confirmed loss. The freeze concerns redemption of a Bitcoin-pegged token used as collateral rather than a failure of Aave itself.

entry.title: NXTT Plans to Sell or Collateralize 5,833 Bitcoin Worth About $449 Million
entry.summary:
Next Technology Holding (NXTT), a Nasdaq-listed software company, said its board has authorized the phased sale or collateralization of roughly 5,833 bitcoin, worth about $449 million. The company cited exchange vulnerabilities, including the Binance attack, and the potential threat quantum computing poses to Bitcoin's cryptography, with CEO Weihong Liu to decide the timing, pricing and size of any transactions.
A Nasdaq-listed corporate treasury publicly citing exchange counterparty risk and quantum risk as grounds to sell or pledge its bitcoin marks a notable shift in how corporate holders frame custody risk. The company said the authorization does not guarantee that any transactions will be completed.
NXTT said its bitcoin is not held at or through Binance, and the authorization covers exchange sales, privately negotiated transactions and bitcoin-collateralized financing. Most of the holdings came from a March 2025 deal in which it acquired 5,000 BTC for total consideration of $158.1 million, about $31,600 per coin, paid in shares, warrants and a cash prepayment.

entry.title: U.S. Spot Ethereum ETFs Hit Record 23-Day Net Outflow Streak Since Launch
entry.summary:
Glassnode reported that U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs have posted 23 consecutive trading days of net outflows, their longest such streak since the funds launched. The on-chain analytics firm said the sustained withdrawals point to weakening demand from traditional-finance investors.
Glassnode linked the streak to a pullback by traditional-finance investors who had accumulated ETH heavily in August and September, making the flow data a gauge of institutional appetite for ether exposure.
A net outflow means redemptions from the funds exceeded new share creation on those trading days, so capital was leaving the ETFs rather than entering them.

entry.title: Binance Plans to Draw Half of SAFU Fund for Breach Losses
entry.summary:
Binance intends to draw down approximately half of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to cover losses stemming from a breach, according to a TOKENPOST report. If carried out, it would be one of the largest deployments of an exchange insurance reserve to date.
SAFU is Binance's last-resort user compensation pool, so a draw of this size signals that the incident's losses are large relative to the reserve the exchange maintains for exactly this purpose.
SAFU was set up in July 2018 and is funded by allocating a percentage of Binance's trading fees; Binance Academy describes the fund as holding crypto assets valued at roughly US$1 billion as of 2026, a figure that fluctuates with the market.

entry.title: THORChain Swaps Remain Paused on 12 Chains After Reported Refund Error
entry.summary:
THORChain's cross-chain swap functionality remains suspended across 12 supported chains following a reported error in its refund mechanism. According to Chainalysis, an Ethereum chain reorganization on the morning of October 31 (EDT) caused THORChain to mistakenly issue a double refund to a user who had deposited 10 ETH, prompting an emergency pause.
The pause blocks cross-chain swaps for all users across most of THORChain's bridges. Chainalysis said the halt also inadvertently delayed the laundering of a significant amount of funds stolen from Binance.
Chainalysis attributed the trigger specifically to an Ethereum chain reorganization, a event in which previously accepted blocks are replaced by a competing chain. No loss figures for the incident have been confirmed in the supplied material.

entry.title: Aave Freezes tBTC Reserve After Threshold Pauses Minting and Redemptions
entry.summary:
Threshold paused minting and redemptions of tBTC, its wrapped-Bitcoin asset, and Aave responded by freezing its tBTC reserve as a precautionary measure against bad debt and collateral risk. The halt affects a wrapped-Bitcoin asset that is integrated across multiple DeFi venues, including Aave's lending market.
Aave's action makes the disruption visible on the largest lending venue where tBTC is used, since a reserve freeze is an asset-specific risk action rather than a routine parameter adjustment. Losses from the Threshold halt have not been quantified.
On Aave, a reserve freeze disables new supply and borrow operations for a single market while leaving repayments and withdrawals active, so existing tBTC positions can still be unwound subject to liquidity. Threshold's bridge relies on a decentralized set of node operators using threshold cryptography to mint and redeem tBTC.

entry.title: Chainalysis Confirms Security Breach, Customer Details Exposed
entry.summary:
Chainalysis has confirmed a security breach in which customer details were exposed, CryptoRank reported. The disclosure makes the blockchain-analytics and compliance vendor the latest third-party provider in the crypto industry to acknowledge a compromise of client information.
Chainalysis supplies transaction-tracing and compliance tooling to exchanges, financial institutions and government agencies, so exposure of its customer details raises data-protection and counterparty-risk questions for those clients.
The report describes the impact as confined to customer details rather than any loss of funds, with the confirmed scope of exposed data described as limited.

entry.title: Kintsu Website Restored, but Team Still Warns Users Not to Connect Wallets
entry.summary:
Kintsu, a liquid staking protocol on the Monad blockchain, said on October 31 that its official website kintsu.xyz has been restored and again points to the project's own infrastructure. The team warned users to keep avoiding the site and not to connect wallets until DNS caches fully refresh and it issues an official security confirmation, noting that some networks may still reach the malicious site for up to an hour.
Security firm Blockaid, which flagged the ongoing front-end attack, advised users not to use the affected decentralized applications while it investigates. Kintsu's warning indicates the risk is not fully cleared even after the domain was restored, because DNS propagation delays can keep serving the malicious version.
According to Blockaid, malicious scripts were injected into the affected sites so that users who clicked "Connect Wallet" could be redirected to a page designed to move their assets. Blockaid said the attack was linked to the StepDrainer toolkit and involved three sites: kintsu, flap and stonkbrokers.

entry.title: ICE Reposts Trade[XYZ] Partnership Announcement, Emphasizing "Plans to Bring" an
entry.summary:
After deleting its earlier post, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) republished its partnership announcement with Trade[XYZ] with amended wording, stating the two parties "plan to bring Hyperliquid-based perps to the U.S." and that any "U.S. regulated versions" remain strictly "subject to regulatory approvals." The revised post says both parties are seeking approvals to launch a new Hyperliquid-based market for KYC-compliant perpetual futures, including approvals needed to support leveraged trading.
The amended language shows the arrangement has not been approved: no U.S. regulated version of the Hyperliquid-based perpetuals market is confirmed to launch, and leveraged trading would require separate regulatory sign-off.
The original announcement was taken down before being reposted in revised form, and the new text consistently frames the U.S. venue as planned rather than approved. Approval is being sought both for the market itself and specifically for leveraged trading.

entry.title: OnePay Now Supports Direct USDC Transfers Into Checking-Account Balance
entry.summary:
Walmart-backed fintech app OnePay announced that users can now send USDC stablecoins directly to their OnePay account, with the funds automatically credited to their existing checking-account balance for bill payments and transfers, without going through an exchange conversion.
The feature removes the exchange-conversion step, letting holders of the dollar-pegged stablecoin apply funds directly to bill payments and transfers inside a Walmart-backed consumer app.
OnePay said the related banking services are provided by Coastal Community Bank or Lead Bank.

entry.title: Websites of several Web3 projects hit by DNS hijacking attack
entry.summary:
Blockaid said in a post on X that it detected DNS hijacking attacks on the websites of several Web3 projects, including Flap and Stonk, so that visitors are redirected to hacker-controlled pages containing malware.
Anyone who reached these project front-ends through the hijacked domains could be routed to attacker infrastructure rather than the genuine site, exposing visitors to malware rather than interacting with the intended application.
The compromise described by Blockaid affects the DNS resolution of the projects' websites rather than their on-chain contracts, and Blockaid did not state in the post how many projects or how many users were affected.

entry.title: Ripple freezes about $200 million in RLUSD as hackers shift to DEXes
entry.summary:
According to Decrypt, Binance co-CEO Yi He said Ripple has frozen approximately $200 million of RLUSD. Suspected attackers are using Uniswap and Aave to swap freezable stablecoins into ETH, and Kamino has paused borrowing in its SOL/BTC markets.
The freeze shows an issuer using its blacklist capability at scale against suspected exploit proceeds, while the attackers' move into ETH via DEXes and lending markets illustrates how freezable stablecoins are being converted into assets issuers cannot freeze. Kamino's halt shows the response extending into Solana lending markets.
The figure comes from Binance co-CEO Yi He as cited by Decrypt, and full loss attribution remains emerging. Kamino's pause applies to borrowing in its SOL/BTC markets.

entry.title: Trezor reveals Malaysian reseller sold wallet with spyware
entry.summary:
Trezor said a Safe 5 hardware wallet purchased from its official Malaysian reseller CryptoBilis in August contained a physical spyware implant — an extra circuit board fitted between the main board and the screen, carrying a cellular module and antenna. According to the user report, the implant reads what the screen displays, including wallet backups, and transmits it over a mobile network whenever the device is plugged in; Trezor has not yet examined the device in its lab but is treating the report as credible and will replace affected wallets.
Trezor's chief commercial officer Danny Sanders said, "We haven't had the device in our lab yet, but we're treating the report as credible, and we'd rather warn people now than wait for confirmation and find out someone lost their funds in the meantime." Buyers who purchased a wallet from CryptoBilis since March 2026 were told to move their funds out and contact Trezor for a replacement.
Trezor said it checked four other CryptoBilis-sourced Trezor wallets and "found no evidence of tampering," and it maintained that "no funds have been reported as stolen" in connection with this report. The described implant works similarly to the spyware previously found in Ledger devices.

entry.title: Jupiter Lend Says Liquidity Crunch Is Delaying Withdrawals
entry.summary:
Jupiter Lend said at 09:01 UTC on 30 October that a "liquidity crunch" was impacting withdrawals from the Solana-based lending protocol, leaving depositors waiting to get their funds out. The protocol stated it has zero exposure to Binance and suffered no losses from the recent Binance security incident.
The disruption directly impairs depositors' ability to exit a major Solana lending venue, and it came within hours of another Solana lender, Kamino, pausing SOL/BTC borrowing after the Binance incident.
Kamino paused SOL/BTC borrowing within hours of the Binance hack, according to Solana Compass. DIA Data lists Jupiter Lend at roughly $2.0 billion in total value locked across 23 pools on one chain and notes the protocol has not published audit reports.

entry.title: Bitcoin Trades Below $80,000 as Long Liquidations Hit $1.34 Billion
entry.summary:
Bitcoin traded below $80,000 as long liquidations reached $1.34 billion, according to The Defiant, reflecting a sharp market-wide deleveraging across crypto derivatives.
The event marks a material market-wide deleveraging in crypto derivatives, with leveraged long positions forced out as bitcoin fell below the $80,000 level.
The $1.34 billion figure refers to long positions, meaning traders betting on higher prices were liquidated during the drop.

entry.title: Polymarket suffers second multimillion-dollar security breach in just four months
entry.summary:
Polymarket has been hit by its second multimillion-dollar security breach in four months, according to CryptoSlate. The incident renews concerns about the prediction market platform's security posture and the safety of user funds.
A second multimillion-dollar breach in four months raises questions about whether the platform's security weaknesses are systemic, given that real user funds are at stake.
The report characterizes the incident as the platform's second multimillion-dollar breach within a four-month window and links it to renewed concerns over user fund safety.

entry.title: Binance investigating hack as suspicious outflows reach up to $5.8 billion
entry.summary:
Binance said it is investigating a security incident after wallets linked to the exchange were drained of at least $5.5 billion on Thursday, with on-chain tallies cited by The Block putting suspicious outflows at up to $5.8 billion across Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron. Binance has not confirmed that user funds were affected, though security researchers widely describe the incident as a hack that would be the largest in the industry's history.
The affected venue is the largest centralized exchange by trading volume, so unresolved questions about the scale of losses and whether customer balances are impaired bear directly on how traders price counterparty and custody risk across the market. Bloomberg reported that the suspected hack triggered emergency asset freezes and sent digital asset prices tumbling.
Tether blacklisted 975.1 million USDT and Circle blacklisted 823 million USDC in the main receiving wallet, and Binance co-CEO Yi He said Ripple also froze about $200 million in RLUSD. The attacker routed funds through Uniswap contracts and borrowed ETH on Aave against USDT collateral — roughly 253,000 ETH (about $570 million) sat in two wallets with no outgoing transfers as of 22:07 UTC — while Aave froze its V3 markets on Ethereum mainnet and Solana-based Kamino paused borrow markets as a precaution.

entry.title: Multiple Polymarket Users Report Stolen Funds as Platform Restricts Trading and
entry.summary:
Multiple Polymarket users reported unauthorized transfers out of their accounts, with some claiming losses of hundreds of thousands of dollars, prompting the platform to enter cancel-only mode, pause relayer actions and temporarily halt trading. Polymarket said one of its third-party providers had been compromised, that the issue affecting Polymarket.com had been identified and fixed, and that the matter has been referred to law enforcement.
The incident triggered a platform-wide trading restriction on one of the largest prediction-market venues, and Polymarket said anyone affected "will be made whole." The root cause remains unconfirmed, with users suspecting a frontend compromise.
Cancel-only mode allowed traders to cancel existing orders but not place new ones, and relayer actions — the service that submits users' signed transactions to the blockchain — were paused; the Predictions Trading API was listed as experiencing a major outage, with Polymarket reporting all systems operational as of 7:05 pm UTC. Security firm Hudson Rock said a DebugBear-hosted script containing wallet-draining code hard-codes the same fallback recipient address as a wallet flagged as the suspected attacker's, which Arkham data showed holding about $2.65 million in POL after multiple USDC.e-to-POL swaps through Relay.

entry.title: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and trade[XYZ] have announced their plan to use
entry.summary:
Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the operator of the New York Stock Exchange, and trade[XYZ] announced on Thursday a plan to use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer for perpetual futures markets serving US traders across crypto, equities, commodities, foreign exchange and other real-world assets, subject to regulatory approvals. Under the structure, Hyperliquid supplies the underlying technology via HIP-3, trade[XYZ] designs and implements the markets, and ICE operates the regulated market and clearing structure.
The arrangement would give US retail traders a regulated route to Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures, while handing ICE a new entry point into retail trading; ICE said the vehicle would run separately from its institutional futures business. OKX CEO Star said the project is being advanced jointly by ICE, trade[XYZ] and OKX, with retail distribution to flow through an ICE-OKX joint venture.
ICE said it has signed a definitive agreement with Trade.xyz and will be the exclusive US operator, with a dedicated clearing structure intended to shield its existing customers — more than 99% of its market participation is institutional — from retail counterparty risk. Existing trade[XYZ] HIP-3 markets will remain unchanged, and HIP-3 deployers remain independent operators responsible for their own deployments.

entry.title: Bitcoin developers rush to fix 3 security flaws after AI uncovers them
entry.summary:
Bitcoin developers moved quickly to patch three security vulnerabilities in the protocol's code after an AI system identified them, CryptoSlate reported. The flaws were uncovered with AI assistance and remediated by developers working on the codebase.
The episode is being framed as a demonstration of both the value and the risks of AI-driven vulnerability research aimed at critical cryptocurrency infrastructure.

entry.title: Singapore Police: Some Retail-Purchased Ledger Hardware Wallets Contained Malicious Components, Total Losses About S$3.5 Million
entry.summary:
Singapore police said on October 28 that some Ledger hardware wallets bought from retail stores in the country contained malicious components able to capture users' recovery phrases or private keys. At least two cases have been reported since September 10, 2026, with combined losses of about S$3.5 million (roughly US$2.7 million).
The affected devices are sold through ordinary retail channels, so users who believe they hold keys offline may still have had their recovery phrases exposed. Police said the unauthorized parties used the captured data to access wallets and move assets without the owners' knowledge or consent.
Singapore police said they have contacted Ledger, which is reviewing the affected cases, and that investigations are ongoing. The announcement did not specify how many devices were affected or which retailers were involved.

entry.title: HTX exits UK, leaving customers to request a 48-hour withdrawal window
entry.summary:
HTX is exiting the UK market and requiring affected customers to request a limited 48-hour withdrawal window instead of retaining normal ongoing access to the exchange. According to CoinTurk reporting, the exit follows a settlement with the UK Financial Conduct Authority over unlawful financial promotions, which the outlet describes as the regulator's first legal action against a crypto firm on those grounds.
UK-based customers lose ongoing access to the platform and must act inside a compressed, request-based window to move their assets. The exit also shows a top-20 exchange withdrawing from a major jurisdiction under regulatory pressure rather than continuing to serve it.
Withdrawal access is request-based rather than automatic, and the window is 48 hours. HTX, formerly known as Huobi, is a Seychelles-based exchange.

entry.title: Strategy reports $19.5 billion in Q3 net income as preferred shareholders approve daily dividends
entry.summary:
Strategy reported $19.5 billion in third-quarter net income and won shareholder approval to move its preferred stocks to daily dividend payments. Per Cointelegraph and Bankless, the change covers four preferred securities — STRC, STRF, STRK and STRD — with daily payouts on STRC starting in November and the other three following in January 2027.
Strategy is the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, so its capital-structure decisions are closely watched by investors using its securities as a proxy for BTC exposure. Shifting preferred dividends from periodic to daily payments changes the cash-flow profile of those instruments and the company's ongoing payment obligations to preferred holders.
The approval was confirmed on Wednesday, Oct. 28, covering a change the company first floated in September. Daily dividends begin on STRC in November, with STRF, STRK and STRD converted in January 2027.

entry.title: ZachXBT: AXIS Insiders Dump ~42M Tokens From Team Multisig, Triggering 40% Crash
entry.summary:
On-chain investigator ZachXBT alleged that suspected Axis Robotics insiders received more than 76 million AXIS tokens (valued at over $12 million) from the team multisig wallet before selling them through decentralized exchanges and depositing funds into Bitget. According to ZachXBT, one insider offloaded roughly 42 million tokens (~5.04 million USDC) directly from the team multisig, triggering a 40% price plunge about one week after AXIS listed on Coinbase, Upbit and Binance.
Axis Robotics pushed back, saying 83.5% of team and investor tokens remain locked in a Binance-co-managed vesting contract with no unlocks for 12 months, and that the sold tokens came from the initial circulating ecosystem allocation handed to an OTC counterparty that it says breached lock-up terms. The company said it has paused ties with that counterparty, initiated legal action and pledged to distribute future ecosystem tokens solely through on-chain vesting.
ZachXBT questioned why it took the team two full days to notice roughly 25% of the TGE float being dumped, and why the team neither stopped the sell-off nor issued a public statement before his post. The two accounts differ on the source of the tokens: ZachXBT attributes the sales to the team multisig, while Axis attributes them to an OTC counterparty's breach.

entry.title: Franklin Templeton Launches Two U.S. Equity-Bitcoin Combination ETFs, Reinvesting Stock Dividends into Bitcoin
entry.summary:
Franklin Templeton announced the Franklin U.S. Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF (FBEQ) and the Franklin U.S. Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF (FIBT), both to be listed on Nasdaq. Each starts with a 95% equity / 5% bitcoin allocation and systematically reinvests dividends from the underlying stocks into bitcoin, with the index reviewing the bitcoin exposure quarterly to keep it as a secondary allocation.
The products give equity investors a dividend-funded route to bitcoin exposure without buying crypto directly, extending a large asset manager's lineup of crypto-related ETFs.
FBEQ covers roughly 500 of the largest U.S. companies by market capitalization with a 0.09% fee, while FIBT covers 100 large non-financial U.S. companies listed on Nasdaq with a 0.19% fee. The quarterly index review is structured by rule to keep bitcoin a minority weight rather than a variable, discretionary position.

entry.title: Datavault AI Discloses $150 Million Bitcoin Withdrawal Blocked, Stock Closes Down 49.6%
entry.summary:
Datavault AI disclosed that roughly 1,328.43 BTC — about $150 million — tied to an equity transaction cannot be withdrawn from a third-party Biconomy wallet. The company said in an 8-K filed October 26 that it requested a withdrawal to an external account in June 2026, and the transfer was still incomplete as of October 26, with the specific reason undisclosed; its stock closed down 49.6% at about $0.067 on October 27.
Datavault AI concluded the funds no longer meet the conditions for recognition as digital assets and should instead be recorded as a subscription receivable from an equity issuance, shown as a deduction from shareholders' equity. The company plans to restate affected financial statements and is reassessing its going-concern status, with the timing of the restatement not yet determined.
Per the filing, Scilex agreed in September 2025 to purchase Datavault AI shares and pre-funded warrants for about 1,328.43 BTC, with the bitcoin credited to its Biconomy wallet via an off-chain transfer. The root cause of the blocked withdrawal has not been disclosed.

entry.title: DTCC Tokenization Service Goes Live, Initially Supporting 34 Securities
entry.summary:
The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation's subsidiary, The Depository Trust Company (DTC), has launched the DTCC Tokenization Service, with 34 securities eligible for tokenization at launch, including selected large-cap Russell 1000 constituents, ETFs and U.S. Treasuries. Tokens are backed 1:1 by securities held in DTC custody, carry the same legal and economic rights as the underlying, use the same CUSIP as the traditional version, and can be transferred peer-to-peer 24/7 between DTC-registered wallets.
DTCC describes the service as creating a "practical path" for tokenized securities adoption, letting DTC participants convert between traditional and tokenized forms while retaining the same ownership rights and investor protections. The partner roster spans custody, wallet and trading infrastructure — BitGo, Blockdaemon, Fireblocks, HashKey, Kaleido, Prometheum, Talos, Temple and Tradeweb — and DTCC said 20 clients have signed agreements to access the service, including Citadel Securities, Citi, Fidelity Investments and JPMorgan.
The service includes built-in compliance controls and near-real-time ownership tracking, and is currently integrated with Canton Network and DTCC's Besu-based private network, with additional networks expected in 2027. Reports of DTC's assets under custody differ — BlockBeats cited roughly $30 trillion while The Defiant cited more than $114 trillion including stocks and ETFs.

entry.title: MetaMask Makes Stellar a Default Network, Existing Accounts Automatically Receive Stellar Addresses
entry.summary:
MetaMask announced a partnership with the Stellar Development Foundation to make Stellar a default network in both its mobile app and browser-extension wallet, with the integration going live on the day of the announcement. All existing MetaMask accounts will automatically derive Stellar addresses from their existing seed phrases with no extra setup, and existing Stellar users can import their original seed phrases to migrate.
MetaMask Chief Product Officer Gal Eldar framed the integration as part of the wallet's "Open Money" strategy, saying the goal is for the same payment infrastructure to serve all users. The default-network placement removes the manual network-addition step that non-EVM chains have typically required in MetaMask.
Stellar addresses are deterministically derived from users' existing mnemonics rather than requiring a new seed phrase, and the change applies to both mobile and extension clients. The announcement did not disclose on-chain volume targets for the integration.

entry.title: Moody's assigns investment-grade ratings to Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin
entry.summary:
Moody's Ratings assigned an A2 long-term deposit rating and a P-1 short-term deposit rating to Ripple USD (RLUSD), the dollar-backed stablecoin issued by Ripple subsidiary Standard Custody & Trust Company, the agency said on Tuesday. A2 is the sixth-highest long-term grade on Moody's scale and P-1 is its top short-term grade.
Moody's said the ratings reflect the quality of RLUSD's reserves, which are held mainly in Treasury bills, other short-term U.S. government assets and cash, most of it with custodian BNY. The action gives the stablecoin an independent credit assessment at a time when Ripple is pitching it to institutional users.
Moody's said RLUSD targets 103% coverage of tokens in circulation, and eligible institutional holders can redeem at par within two business days; the agency also flagged that Standard Custody is not a bankruptcy-remote entity and that RLUSD holders do not currently have a direct ownership interest in the reserves. The ratings were requested by the issuer, and Moody's noted that the GENIUS Act, due to take effect in 2027, will exclude required reserves from an issuer's bankruptcy estate.

entry.title: BNY offers XRP custody, but only 1 rollout type exists
entry.summary:
BNY (Bank of New York Mellon) has begun offering custody services for XRP, according to CryptoSlate, extending its institutional digital-asset custody coverage to the asset. The offering currently exists in only one rollout type, a narrower scope than a full multi-model launch.
The report frames the addition as an expansion of institutional custody support for XRP, giving bank-grade custody coverage to an asset that previously sat outside this particular channel.
The rollout is limited to a single custody type, which tempers the scope of the announcement even as it adds a major bank to XRP's custody line-up.

entry.title: Iron Fish: Abnormal minting of wIRON on Base, do not buy or use the cross-chain bridge for now
entry.summary:
Iron Fish said on Oct. 28 that it is investigating abnormal minting of wIRON, the wrapped version of its token on Base, and has asked cross-chain bridge provider ChainPort to carry out an urgent review. The team told users not to buy wIRON on Base or use the related bridge until further notice because full 1:1 reserve backing can no longer be guaranteed.
By its own statement, Iron Fish can no longer guarantee that wIRON on Base is fully backed 1:1, which puts the redemption value of the wrapped asset in question while the investigation continues.
Iron Fish said it will publish further updates once the facts are confirmed; the cause of the abnormal minting has not been disclosed. The advisory covers both buying wIRON on Base and using the associated bridge.

entry.title: Robinhood posts record $1.4 billion revenue, but a 14% profit drop exposes hidden portfolio losses
entry.summary:
Robinhood reported record revenue of $1.4 billion alongside a 14% drop in profit, with the results tied to losses in its own portfolio holdings. The online brokerage's shares came under pressure after the report, falling about 6.6% in pre-market trading from a $95 close on October 27 to $88.
The quarter shows Robinhood's top line expanding even as profitability weakens, and the stock reaction indicates investors are weighing the profit miss over the record revenue.
Crypto transaction revenue fell 55% year-over-year to $120 million in the third quarter ended September 30, though it still topped Street forecasts. Coverage of the results also pointed to declining interest income and rising expenses weighing on profit despite record trading activity in stocks, options and prediction markets.

entry.title: Coinbase Vendor Incident Exposes The Weak Link Behind Private Keys
entry.summary:
DailyCoin published an analysis arguing that a third-party vendor incident at Coinbase exposes the security weaknesses contractors can introduce to exchange private-key and customer infrastructure. Search excerpts describe the vendor as analytics provider Amplitude, which experienced a security incident affecting a small subset of Coinbase customer contact data, while Coinbase said it found no evidence of unauthorized access to its systems.
The episode highlights how third-party vendors can become an indirect exposure path for exchange customer data, even when the exchange says its own systems were not breached.
The described exposure involved customer contact data rather than private keys, and Coinbase said funds were unaffected. No loss figure or confirmed private-key compromise has been disclosed.

entry.title: Kamino Opens USDC Loans Against Backpack Tokenized Stocks
entry.summary:
Kamino, a lending and liquidity protocol on Solana, has launched USDC loans collateralized by Backpack-issued tokenized stocks, letting borrowers draw dollar liquidity against tokenized equity positions instead of selling them. The product marks a new use of tokenized equities as DeFi loan collateral.
The launch makes tokenized equities usable as collateral inside an onchain credit market, extending real-world asset integration and cross-market composability on Solana. It also puts equity-price and off-market-hours risk directly into a DeFi lending pool.
Backpack issues its tokenized equities through Backpack Securities, with Sunrise handling custody and token issuance, and the tokens can be redeemed for underlying value — a mechanism described as creating a price floor relative to the represented asset. Kamino positions itself as an open-source credit and liquidity protocol on Solana that supports borrowing against onchain collateral through transparent markets.

entry.title: ENSv2 Officially Launches on Ethereum Mainnet
entry.summary:
ENSv2 went live on the Ethereum mainnet on October 27, introducing hierarchical registries and a more granular permission model under which a single name can act as an independent on-chain registry, letting communities and organizations define their own subdomain issuance rules and delegate management by zone. The release also updates how names are resolved, adds support for shared record links, and ships a new ENS App for general users plus an ENS Explorer for developers.
ENS says its ecosystem now covers more than 36 million domains across over 600 applications, and that existing .eth domains will continue to work without re-registration, with users able to voluntarily upgrade to ENSv2 in the ENS App starting today. The permission changes shift control over subdomain rules and ownership management from a single global registry to individual name owners.
After upgrading all eligible domains, users can claim a commemorative ENSv2 NFT designed by artist Polyhop, one per wallet, subject to Ethereum network gas fees. 1inch, MetaMask, Safe, Uniswap, PayPal, Venmo and OpenSea are among the applications already adapting to ENSv2.
